root_cause.text: In `arm64/mm/contpte.c`, `contpte_ptep_set_access_flags()` used the gathered `ptep_get()` view of a contiguous PTE block to decide a no-op, but that view ORs AF/dirty across all sub-PTEs so a sibling’s state could mask a target sub-PTE that still lacked the needed `PTE_AF` or `PTE_RDONLY` update in hardware, causing access-fault loops on walkers that inspect descriptors individually.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `contpte_all_subptes_match_access_flags()` to compare raw per-sub-PTE values against the requested AF/dirty/write state and replaces `if (pte_val(orig_pte) == pte_val(entry))` with a full CONT-block check; the commit text explicitly says `ptep_get() ORs AF/dirty from all sub-PTEs`, which could make `contpte_ptep_set_access_flags()` return 0 even though the target sub-PTE still had `PTE_RDONLY` set.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper to ensure all sub-PTEs in a contiguous mapping share the same access flags before access-flag updates are applied.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function named contpte_all_subptes_match_access_flags() was added. It aligns the given PTE pointer down to the start of the contiguous PTE block, defines a comparison mask of PTE_RDONLY, PTE_AF, PTE_WRITE, and PTE_DIRTY, computes the masked value of the provided entry, then iterates over all CONT_PTES sub-PTEs and compares each sub-PTE's masked value against the entry; it returns false on the first mismatch and true if all match.
intent_record.how: This enables the code to verify that every sub-PTE in a contiguous PTE block already matches the access-flag state represented by the target entry, ignoring PFN differences. At runtime, this can prevent incorrect access-flag updates from being applied when the contiguous entries are not uniformly aligned in their AF/dirty/write state, improving correctness of subsequent contpte access-flag handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix contiguous PTE access-flag updates to check raw sub-PTE state and avoid false no-op decisions when only sibling entries have been updated.
intent_record.what: The function `contpte_ptep_set_access_flags()` no longer builds `orig_pte` from `pte_mknoncont(ptep_get(ptep))` and compares that gathered value directly against `entry` to decide a no-op. Instead, it first calls `contpte_all_subptes_match_access_flags(ptep, entry)` and returns 0 only if every sub-PTE in the contiguous block already matches the requested access flags/write permission. If not, it then sets `orig_pte` from `pte_mknoncont(__ptep_get(ptep))` using the raw target PTE rather than the gathered view. The surrounding comments were expanded to explain the new matching logic and why raw per-PTE values are needed.
intent_record.how: This changes the access-flag update path so that a contiguous PTE block is not incorrectly treated as unchanged when only sibling entries have been updated. It prevents false no-op decisions caused by aggregated AF/dirty state from `ptep_get()`, ensuring the target sub-PTE gets updated when it still lacks AF or still has PTE_RDONLY set. As a result, hardware or walkers that inspect individual descriptors will see consistent attributes across the whole contiguous range, and write/read faults caused by stale target sub-PTE bits are avoided.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause: they fix contpte access-flag handling by checking raw sub-PTE state instead of the aggregated ptep_get() view, preventing sibling entries from masking a sub-PTE that still needs AF/readonly updates.

candidates.rationale: This uses the aggregated ptep_get() view of the contiguous PTE block, which can OR access/dirty state across sibling entries and therefore misrepresent the actual target sub-PTE state.
This no-op check is based on the potentially distorted aggregated PTE view, so it can incorrectly skip the access-flag update even when the specific sub-PTE still needs hardware AF/RDONLY changes.
Returning early here is the direct effect of the faulty comparison; it prevents applying the needed access-flag update and can leave a sub-PTE in a state that continues to fault.

vuln_statements.explanation: This no-op check compares the aggregated contiguous-PTE view against the requested entry, so sibling sub-PTE updates can mask the target PTE’s missing AF or read-only state and incorrectly skip the needed hardware update.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `contpte_ptep_set_access_flags()`. The code does `orig_pte = pte_mknoncont(ptep_get(ptep));` and then uses the gathered view to decide a no-op: `if (pte_val(orig_pte) == pte_val(entry)) return 0;`. The root cause says this `ptep_get()`-based gathered view ORs AF/dirty across all sub-PTEs, so a sibling can mask a target sub-PTE that still needs an update. That exact pattern exists here. The fix is not present because the function still relies on the aggregated `ptep_get()` result for the equality/no-op check, rather than checking or updating the individual sub-PTE state before returning. The later code does handle updating all PTEs when `pte_write(orig_pte) == pte_write(entry)`, but that does not change the vulnerable early-return decision.
